Aniseed Anice; Anis; Anis, fruit d’; Anís, semilla de; Anis Verde; Anis Vert; Anise; Anise Fruit; Anisi fructus; Ánizstermés (fruit); Anyžiu ̨ vai- siai (fruit); Anýzový plod (fruit); Owoc anyz ̇u (fruit). Pharmacopoeias. In Eur. (see p.vii). Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Aniseed; Anisi Fructus). The whole dried fruit of Pimpinella anisum, containing not less than 2% v/w of essential oil. It has an odour reminiscent of anethole. Protect from light. Profile Aniseed is carminative and mildly expectorant; it is used mainly as anise oil or as preparations of the oil. It may cause contact dermatitis, probably due to its anethole content. Aniseed is the source of anise oil (below). ◊ References. 1. Chandler RF, Hawkes D. Aniseed—a spice, a flavor, a drug. Can Pharm J 1984; 117: 28–9. 2. Fraj J, et al. Occupational asthma induced by aniseed. Allergy 1996; 51: 337–9. 3. Garcia-Gonzalez JJ, et al. Occupational rhinoconjunctivitis and food allergy because of aniseed sensitization. Ann Allergy Asth- ma Immunol 2002; 88: 518–22.
